assessment: All four inline comments are pedagogically necessary and non-duplicative: they respectively separate samples from an unobserved path, externalize the record contract, show that sample rate changes physical interpretation without changing codes, and separate physical input, integer representation, calibration, and clipping. Each is a one-claim diagram with short labels, so the existing raw-SVG plan is compatible with the figure-artist tier rules.

figures.necessity: The opening misconception is visual: readers routinely infer a continuous curve from dots. Prose alone cannot make the deliberately blank between-sample regions as immediate.
figures.visual_claim: Sampling retains values at declared instants; the discrete sequence contains no represented path between those instants.
figures.layout: One 640-wide, two-panel comparison. Left: a minimal microphone glyph, a muted smooth candidate voltage path, and eight amber sample instants. Right: the same eight amber stem-and-dot samples on an integer n axis, with no connecting line and a labeled blank interval between two dots.
required_labels_data: Left labels: one possible continuous input x_c(t); sample instants t_n.
Right labels: discrete sequence x[n]; sample index n; not represented by x[n].
Use amber #e2903a only for retained samples; use currentColor at reduced opacity for the candidate continuous path. Do not encode the distinction by color alone.
source_basis: Lyons §1.1: a discrete sequence is defined only at integer indices and has no defined values between samples.
Schaedler Lessons 3–4: sample values need a sampling period and admit multiple continuous histories.

accessibility.alt: Two panels show a possible continuous microphone trace sampled at eight instants and the resulting eight unconnected discrete samples, with the gaps labeled as not represented by x[n].
accessibility.caption: The samples retain values at eight instants; they do not retain the path between them.
accessibility.needs: Keep the no-connecting-line distinction geometric, not color-only; make the blank-gap annotation readable in source order after the right-panel title.

key_image_role.role: Inline misconception repair at the first definition.

render_qa: Use a viewBox near 0 0 640 280 with no fixed width or height; centered display must remain legible near 700 px.
All labels are at least 12 px system-ui; axes, stems, and glyph remain distinct in light and dark renders.
No line, implied fill, or arrow joins the right-panel sample dots.
The left candidate path visibly passes through all eight sample instants without being mistaken for retained data.

Render with npm run figure -- content/courses/digital-signal-processing/lessons/sampled-sequences/figures/microphone-samples.svg and --dark; inspect both previews for clipping, label collisions, and currentColor contrast.

figures.necessity: The four-layer contract is the lesson's organizing device. A literal aligned ledger lets readers see that index, time, code, calibrated amplitude, and acquisition claims are separate fields rather than interchangeable axis labels.
figures.visual_claim: A stored code array becomes physical evidence only after separate index, time, amplitude-calibration, and acquisition declarations are attached.
figures.layout: One 640-wide ledger of five aligned cards or columns, read left to right: index, physical time, integer code, calibrated value, acquisition. A compact correction strip below crosses out n (ms) and replaces it with sample index n or time t=nT_s (ms).
required_labels_data: Index: n=0,1,...,7 and unit: none.
Time: t_n=t_0+nT_s and unit: s or ms.
Code: c[n]=[0,1,0,-1,0,1,0,-1] and representation: integer code.
Calibration: x[n]=(c[n]-c_0)q and unit example: V; do not invent numeric q or c_0 before the prose declares them.
Acquisition fields: f_s, analog filter/passband, converter range, clipping checked.
Color-bind amber #e2903a to index n, blue #4c8dd6 to physical time nT_s, and green #5aa46a to calibrated amplitude x[n]; introduce each color in its named header.
source_basis: Lyons §1.1: sample index and amplitude pattern do not determine physical frequency without the sample period.
Orfanidis §§1.1–1.7: sampling, conversion, physical units, and acquisition stages are distinct.
The research brief notation ledger reserves n for a dimensionless index and nT_s for physical time.

accessibility.alt: A five-part ledger maps integer index n to physical time, converter code, calibrated voltage, and acquisition metadata, while crossing out the incorrect axis label n in milliseconds.
accessibility.caption: Index, time, code, calibration, and acquisition are separate fields in the record contract.
accessibility.needs: Every colored role must also have a text header; the incorrect axis must be identifiable by the strike mark and correction text, not by a warning color alone.

key_image_role.role: Inline summary of the lesson's record-contract schema.

render_qa: Use a viewBox near 0 0 640 300; all five columns remain at least 108 px wide with 12 px minimum text.
No formula or acquisition label wraps into a neighboring card; brackets, subscripts, and ellipses render as intended without TeX source artifacts.
The crossed-out n (ms) strip remains visibly subordinate to the ledger and does not introduce a fourth palette hue.
Reading order is unambiguous left to right, and all text meets contrast requirements in both themes.
Render the SVG in light and dark with npm run figure, inspect the PNGs, and reject any version whose smallest acquisition label is not readable at the centered lesson width.

figures.necessity: This is the lesson's concrete counterexample and configured key image. It makes the sixfold change in physical time and modeled frequency visible while holding every stored code and sample index fixed.
figures.visual_claim: The same eight codes and four-sample pattern represent different sample spans and modeled physical frequencies when only the sampling rate changes.
figures.layout: Two near-identical 300-wide panels joined by one bold central comparison arrow. Both show the same eight stems on n=0,...,7. The left metadata is amber for 8 kHz; the right metadata is blue for 48 kHz. A central tally states f_s times 6, modeled f_0 times 6, and sample-span divided by 6.
required_labels_data: Shared codes: [0,1,0,-1,0,1,0,-1]; shared period in index: 4 samples.
Left: f_s=8 kHz; T_s=125 microseconds; last sample/sample-span=0.875 ms; modeled tone f_0=2 kHz.
Right: f_s=48 kHz; T_s=20.833 microseconds; last sample/sample-span approximately 0.146 ms; modeled tone f_0=12 kHz.
Use the exact term sample-span or last sample time, not ambiguous duration; the half-open record interval is intentionally not part of this one-claim comparison.
Use identical plot geometry and code labels in both panels; only rate-dependent metadata changes.
source_basis: Lyons §1.1: absolute frequency requires the sample period or rate, not merely the plotted sample pattern.
Research brief worked case: the identical eight-number array has 0.875 ms span and 2 kHz modeled frequency at 8 kHz, versus about 0.146 ms and 12 kHz at 48 kHz.

accessibility.alt: Identical eight-sample code plots are labeled at 8 kHz and 48 kHz; the higher rate shortens the last-sample time from 0.875 to about 0.146 milliseconds and raises the modeled tone from 2 to 12 kilohertz.
accessibility.caption: Changing only the sample rate multiplies modeled physical frequency by six and divides sample-span by six.
accessibility.needs: Repeat all changed values as text in each panel and in the central tally so the comparison does not depend on amber-versus-blue color.

key_image_role.role: Configured course.yaml key image and the first build priority; it must communicate the lesson thesis without surrounding prose and must clear the current missing-key-image validation error.

render_qa: Use a viewBox near 0 0 640 320 with pixel-identical plot frames and stem locations across panels.
The literal code pattern, 8 kHz/48 kHz labels, 0.875 ms/0.146 ms values, and 2 kHz/12 kHz values remain legible at card and centered lesson widths.
The central times-6/divide-by-6 tally has no ambiguous arrow direction and does not imply the code amplitudes changed.
No panel is clipped when used as the key image; the comparison remains balanced without relying on the MDX caption.

figures.necessity: The prose distinguishes codes from volts and warns that clipping destroys information. A left-to-right acquisition chain locates exactly where filtering, sampling, quantization, storage, and later calibration enter that claim.
figures.visual_claim: The ADC stores integer codes after filtering, sampling, and quantization; calibrated volts are derived from those codes, while clipped input information cannot be recovered by calibration.
figures.layout: One 640-wide left-to-right pipeline with five compact stages and straight data-flow arrows: microphone voltage, analog antialias filter, sampler, quantizer, integer buffer. A thin lower arrow maps the buffer through calibration to x[n], and a small clipping stop marker attaches only to the quantizer.
required_labels_data: Input: microphone voltage x_c(t), unit V.
Filter: analog antialias filter; stated passband B with B<f_s/2.
Sampler: t_n=t_0+nT_s and f_s=1/T_s.
Quantizer: declared range [V_min,V_max], step q V/code, and clipping loses information.
Buffer: integer code c[n].
Calibration below: x[n]=(c[n]-c_0)q in volts; label this as an estimate from an unsaturated code, not an inverse of clipping.
Use amber #e2903a for the physical analog path, blue #4c8dd6 for the stored code path, and green #5aa46a only for the calibrated-voltage result; name every role in text.
source_basis: Orfanidis §1.7: analog antialias prefilter, A/D conversion, digital processing, D/A conversion, and analog postfilter are distinct roles.
Smith Chapters 3–4: conversion produces literal numeric arrays whose representation and calibration constrain physical interpretation.
Lesson prose: x[n]=(c[n]-c_0)q and a saturated code cannot reveal the larger changing input that produced it.

accessibility.alt: A microphone voltage passes through an analog antialias filter, sampler, quantizer, and integer-code buffer; a separate calibration maps unsaturated codes back to voltage, while a clipping marker shows lost information.
accessibility.caption: Sampling and quantization create codes; calibration assigns volts, but it cannot undo clipping.
accessibility.needs: Use arrow direction and explicit stage titles in addition to color; the clipping warning must be adjacent to the quantizer and stated in words.

key_image_role.role: Inline architecture that anchors the code-versus-voltage section.

render_qa: Use a viewBox near 0 0 640 250; arrows point only right, and the lower calibration arrow never crosses a pipeline label.
All five boxes have consistent height, 3–6 px corner radius, and at least 12 px system-ui labels.
The quantizer range, q unit, buffer c[n], and calibration equation remain legible without crowding; no fourth hue or decorative icon is introduced.
The diagram does not imply the digital buffer contains volts or that calibration can recover clipped magnitude.
Render light and dark SVG previews and inspect for arrowhead clipping, formula collisions, and low-contrast muted text before page-level preview.
